title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 96
paragraphs: On all the ships there served as fighting men Persians, Medes, or Sacae. Of the ships, those that sailed best were supplied by the Phoenicians, and among the Phoenicians the best were those of Sidon. Over all these men, and over those of them who were assigned to the land army as well, there were native chieftains for each people; but since the inquiry does not oblige me, I make no mention of them in passing — first because the chieftains of each nation were not persons worthy of mention, and second because within each nation there were as many chieftains as there were cities. These men went with the expedition not as commanders but like the rest, serving as slaves; for the generals who held absolute power and commanded the various nations — that is, those who were Persians — have already been named by me.
